reductionDefinition: Karp's Reduction from Subset Sum to Partition
source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.

reductionFrom.formalDefinition: Subset Sum = <S, T> | S is a set of positive integers and there exists a subset of S, K where the sum of K's elements equals T
reductionFrom.problemDefinition: The problem is to determine whether there exists a sum of elements that totals to the number T.
reductionFrom.inputDescription: S, a set of integers, and T, a target sum
reductionFrom.outputDescription: True or False, whether some subset of S sums to T
reductionFrom.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
reductionFrom.instanceFormat: Format: {(S,T) | S subset int, T is int} Example: ({1,7,12,15},28)

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for Subset Sum

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: This is a verifier for Subset Sum

defaultVisualization.visualizationDefinition: Draws the numbers as items and the chosen ones as a bar against the target T, and shows the selected solver trying subsets until one adds up to exactly T.

solver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for Subset Sum

reductionTo.formalDefinition: Partition = <S, I> | S is a set of positive integers and there exists a subset of S, I where the sum of I's elements equals the sum of elements not in set I
reductionTo.problemDefinition: The partition problem is the task of deciding whether a given multiset S of positive integers can be partitioned into two subsets S1 and S2 such that the sum of the numbers in S1 equals the sum of the numbers in S2
reductionTo.inputDescription: S, a multiset of positive integers
reductionTo.outputDescription: True or False, whether S can be partitioned into two subsets with equal sum
reductionTo.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
reductionTo.instanceFormat: Format: {N | N subset int} (a multiset of positive integers S; a number written twice counts twice) Example: {3,5,7,8,9,10}
reductionTo.certificateFormat: Format: (S1),(S2) | S1,S2 partition S exactly (each element used once), sum(S1) = sum(S2) Example: (5,7,9),(3,8,10)

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for the Partition problem

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: This is a verifier for the Partition problem

defaultVisualization.visualizationDefinition: This is a default visualization for Partition

solver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for the Partition problem
